plan:
EXPERIMENT DESIGN — QuaRot end-to-end 4-bit quantization: effect on LLaMa-2 prefill and decoding performance.

DESIGN-ONLY. No experiment was run and none is claimed to have been run. All quantitative figures below are design targets drawn from the literature (QuaRot, Dettmers et al., 2024; LLaMa-2 tech report), not measurements. This environment has no GPU, no ML packages, and no network; nothing here can execute the design.

--- 1. QUESTION ---
How does QuaRot's end-to-end 4-bit quantization affect the prefill and decoding performance (latency, throughput, memory) of LLaMa-2, relative to full precision and relative to a weight-only 4-bit scheme, and at what quality cost?

--- 2. STATEMENT OF ASSUMPTIONS (up front; each is load-bearing) ---
A1. Hardware = NVIDIA A100-80GB (QuaRot paper's hardware). All memory/throughput targets assume A100. H100 and batched/served decode are sensitivity considerations only, not primary conditions.
A2. Decode evaluated at batch=1 (single-stream autoregressive, the memory-bandwidth-bound regime).
A3. Prefill evaluated over a prompt-length sweep: 512 / 2048 / 4096 tokens.
A4. Full-precision baseline = BF16 (LLaMa-2's native dtype, and the paper's comparison point).
A5. KEY RISK: "end-to-end 4-bit" is interpreted as the published QuaRot scheme — 4-bit (FP4) weights AND 4-bit (FP4) activations AND 4-bit KV-cache, via Hadamard rotation + incoherence processing. If the intended scope were weights-only 4-bit, the memory/accuracy story narrows materially: the KV-cache and activation savings (a large share of the total memory win) disappear, peak-memory reduction shrinks, and the "no accuracy loss" claim weakens. This is the single assumption that, if wrong, changes the design most.
A6. A light accuracy block is in scope: the speed/memory wins only matter if the model still works; "performance" without a quality bound is misleading.

--- 3. CONDITIONS (cells) ---
Model sizes (primary cells): LLaMa-2 7B and LLaMa-2 13B.
Model sizes (secondary/conditional cell): LLaMa-2 70B — FEASIBILITY CAVEAT: 70B is where 4-bit memory savings are most dramatic and where QuaRot's "fits on a single node" claim matters most, but it is the costliest cell; in BF16 it needs ~140GB of weights (multi-GPU) whereas QuaRot-4bit targets single-node residency. Include 70B only if a multi-GPU/single-node A100 setup is available; otherwise treat it as a scaling check reported from the paper rather than a primary measured cell.

Quantization conditions (identical across every model size):
- C0 (primary control): BF16 full precision.
- C1 (treatment): QuaRot end-to-end 4-bit (FP4 weights + FP4 activations + 4-bit KV-cache).
- C2 (secondary control): GPTQ weight-only 4-bit (weights quantized, activations and KV-cache kept in higher precision). This isolates QuaRot's end-to-end advantage: C1 vs C0 shows the total effect of end-to-end 4-bit; C1 vs C2 shows the marginal gain from also quantizing activations and KV-cache (the part GPTQ leaves unquantized).

--- 4. METRICS ---
Prefill (compute-bound, parallel over the sequence):
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT), ms.
- Prefill throughput, prompt tokens/s.
- Peak GPU memory during prompt load, GB.
Evaluated at each of the 512 / 2048 / 4096 prompt lengths.

Decoding (memory-bandwidth-bound, batch=1):
- Time-per-output-token (TPOT / inter-token latency), ms.
- Decode throughput, generated tokens/s.
- Time-to-complete a fixed decode length (e.g., 256 generated tokens), s.

Shared across conditions:
- Peak GPU memory, GB: model weights + KV-cache footprint.
- Quality block (A6): (i) WikiText-2 perplexity; (ii) one or two zero-shot probes (ARC-e and HellaSwag as the default pair, PIQA optional). Quality is reported per quantization condition, not per prompt length.

Rationale for the split: prefill is FLOP-bound and benefits little from weight compression; decoding is bandwidth-bound and benefits most. Reporting them separately is the core of the question.

--- 5. CONTROLS AND EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN ---
- Same hardware (A100-80GB), same prompt corpus, same prompt-length sweep, and same decode length across C0/C1/C2 within each model size, so differences are attributable to quantization, not data or config.
- Fixed prompt set (deterministic, versioned) so prefill/decode are paired across conditions on identical inputs.
- Warm-up runs discarded; then repeated measurement runs (e.g., 5–10) per (condition, prompt-length) to capture variance.
- Same inference stack / kernel path for all conditions where possible; note any kernel differences (e.g., QuaRot's custom dequant kernels vs GPTQ's) as a confound to record, not hide.
- Accuracy (ppl, zero-shot) computed once per condition on a fixed eval split.

--- 6. ANALYSIS PLAN ---
- Paired comparisons across conditions on the same prompt corpus (not independent samples).
- Report mean + 95% CI via bootstrap (resampling over runs and prompts). Small n -> bootstrap CIs and paired t-tests; state n honestly rather than over-modeling.
- Primary effect quantification: relative speedup (×) and relative memory reduction (%) of C1 (QuaRot) vs C0 (BF16), reported SEPARATELY for prefill and decode; plus C1 vs C2 to isolate the end-to-end contribution.
- Accuracy delta: Δperplexity and Δtask-accuracy of C1 vs C0 (and vs C2).
- Pre-registered "meaningful effect" threshold (set before looking at results, so "meaningful" is not post-hoc): e.g., a decode speedup ≥ ~1.5× OR a peak-memory reduction ≥ ~50% of BF16, with quality degradation bounded at ≤ ~0.5 ppl and ≤ ~1% absolute zero-shot accuracy. Report whether the design's targets are met against this bar.
- Expected direction (literature-based, to be confirmed): large decode speedup and large memory reduction at near-flat quality; smaller prefill gain; C1 ≥ C2 on memory with comparable-or-better accuracy.

--- 7. FEASIBILITY NOTE (honest) ---
- All numbers in this design are literature-derived design targets, NOT measurements. No run occurred and none is claimed.
- This environment cannot execute the design: no GPU (nvidia-smi fails), no ML packages (no torch/transformers/quarot), network disabled.
- Feasible core if actually run: 7B on a single A100-80GB with the 512/2048/4096 sweep and a short fixed prompt corpus, 5–10 repeated runs per cell, single seed. 13B fits on one 80GB A100 in 4-bit/BF16 (BF16 13B ≈ 26GB weights). 70B is the conditional cell (see §3 caveat).
- KEY RISK (most design-breaking if wrong): if "end-to-end 4-bit" were actually intended as weights-only, the memory/accuracy story narrows — the KV-cache and activation quantization (a large share of QuaRot's total memory win) would be out of scope, the peak-memory reduction would shrink, and the near-zero-accuracy-loss claim would weaken. The C1-vs-C2 contrast is designed to expose exactly this, but the headline claim depends on A5 holding.
- Sensitivity (not primary): H100 would shift absolute throughput/memory and the "single-node" framing; batched/served decode (batch>1) would change the decode metric and memory model substantially.

## 1. Workspace inspection — what's actually there

`/workspace` contains **exactly one file**: `task.json` (405 bytes). No QuaRot source, no LLaMa-2 checkpoint metadata, no benchmarking scripts, no README, no configs.

`task.json` itself confirms the situation:
```json
"context": "Design an experiment ... Do not claim that an experiment was run.",
"documents": { "track.md": "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required." }
```

Environment probe:
- Python 3.14.4; **no GPU** (`nvidia-smi` fails — no driver); 224 CPUs.
- **No ML packages installed** (no torch/transformers/quarot/accelerate/flash-attn); network **disabled**, so nothing can be installed anyway.

**Bottom line: we are working from literature knowledge alone.** The design must be self-contained and cite the published QuaRot setup (Dettmers et al., "QuaRot: New Frontiers in Low-Bit LLMs," 2024) as the anchor. I cannot claim any run happened and shouldn't.

## 2. Proposed skeleton (high-level, reasoning exposed)

**(a) Model sizes.** I'd target **LLaMa-2 7B and 13B** as the primary, with **70B as a secondary/conditional** cell.
- 7B/13B are the sizes QuaRot's paper actually benchmarks end-to-end, so results are directly comparable to the source (anchor for validity).
- 70B is where 4-bit memory savings are most dramatic and where QuaRot's "fits in one node" claim matters — but it's the costliest cell, so I'd make it a *conditional* inclusion rather than a hard requirement.
- Fork: if budget is tight → 7B only as the "feasible core" and 13B/70B as scaling checks.

**(b) Metrics — prefill vs decoding.** These are genuinely different regimes, so I split them:
- **Prefill** (prompt processing, compute-bound, parallel over the sequence): *time-to-first-token (TTFT)* and *prefill throughput (prompt tokens/s)*. Memory peak during prompt load.
- **Decoding** (autoregressive, memory-bandwidth-bound, batch of 1 per step): *per-token latency (ITL/TPOT)* and *decode throughput (generated tokens/s)*.
- **Shared:** peak GPU memory / model + KV-cache footprint (bytes), and **quality**: perplexity on WikiText-2 + a small downstream probe (e.g., a few zero-shot tasks: ARC-e, HellaSwag, PIQA) so we can report the *speed/accuracy tradeoff*, not just speed.
- Justification: prefill is FLOP-bound and decode is bandwidth-bound, so a quantization that shrinks weights helps decode (less memory traffic) more than prefill; separating them is the whole point of the question. Accuracy is required because "performance" without quality is misleading.
- Fork: do we report quality at all, or is the researcher's "performance" strictly latency/memory? I lean **include a light accuracy block** as it's cheap relative to the value.

**(c) Baseline / controls.**
- **Primary baseline: BF16 (full precision)** — this is the cleanest "effect of quantization" contrast and matches how QuaRot reports deltas.
- **Secondary comparison: a competing 4-bit scheme (GPTQ or AWQ)** — to show QuaRot's advantage (esp. activation-quantization / KV-cache quantization and no accuracy loss) rather than just "4-bit vs 16-bit." I'd pick **GPTQ** as the most-cited 4-bit weight-only baseline; AWQ as a lighter alternative.
- Controls: same hardware, same prompt set, same batch/seq config across all conditions; repeated runs for variance.
- Fork: BF16 vs FP16 as the FP baseline (BF16 is the LLaMa-2 native dtype — I default to BF16).

**(d) Analysis plan.**
- Paired comparisons across conditions on the *same* prompt corpus; report mean + CI (e.g., bootstrap 95% CI) per metric.
- **Effect framing:** relative speedup (×) and relative memory reduction (%) of QuaRot-4bit vs BF16, decomposed into prefill vs decode; plus accuracy delta (Δppl, Δtask-acc) to bound the cost.
- **Meaningful effect:** a pre-registered threshold (e.g., ≥1.5× decode speedup or ≥50% memory reduction with ≤0.5 ppl / ≤1% task-acc degradation) — I'd set this explicitly so "meaningful" isn't post-hoc.
- Statistical treatment: since n is small (few runs), I'd use bootstrap CIs / paired t-tests and be honest about the small n rather than heavy modeling.

## 3. Consequential assumptions & uncertainties (each would change the design if wrong)

How does QuaRot's end-to-end 4-bit quantization affect the prefill and decoding performance (latency, throughput, memory) of LLaMa-2, relative to full precision and relative to a weight-only 4-bit scheme, and at what quality cost?

--- 2. STATEMENT OF ASSUMPTIONS (up front; each is load-bearing) ---

A2. Decode evaluated at batch=1 (single-stream autoregressive, the memory-bandwidth-bound regime).
A3. Prefill evaluated over a prompt-length sweep: 512 / 2048 / 4096 tokens.
A4. Full-precision baseline = BF16 (LLaMa-2's native dtype, and the paper's comparison point).
A5. KEY RISK: "end-to-end 4-bit" is interpreted as the published QuaRot scheme — 4-bit (FP4) weights AND 4-bit (FP4) activations AND 4-bit KV-cache, via Hadamard rotation + incoherence processing. If the intended scope were weights-only 4-bit, the memory/accuracy story narrows materially: the KV-cache and activation savings (a large share of the total memory win) disappear, peak-memory reduction shrinks, and the "no accuracy loss" claim weakens. A6. A light accuracy block is in scope: the speed/memory wins only matter if the model still works; "performance" without a quality bound is misleading.

--- 3. CONDITIONS (cells) ---
Model sizes (primary cells): LLaMa-2 7B and LLaMa-2 13B.
Model sizes (secondary/conditional cell): LLaMa-2 70B — FEASIBILITY CAVEAT: 70B is where 4-bit memory savings are most dramatic and where QuaRot's "fits on a single node" claim matters most, but it is the costliest cell; in BF16 it needs ~140GB of weights (multi-GPU) whereas QuaRot-4bit targets single-node residency. Include 70B only if a multi-GPU/single-node A100 setup is available; otherwise treat it as a scaling check reported from the paper rather than a primary measured cell.

Quantization conditions (identical across every model size):
- C0 (primary control): BF16 full precision.

This isolates QuaRot's end-to-end advantage: C1 vs C0 shows the total effect of end-to-end 4-bit; C1 vs C2 shows the marginal gain from also quantizing activations and KV-cache (the part GPTQ leaves unquantized).

--- 4. METRICS ---
Prefill (compute-bound, parallel over the sequence):
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT), ms.
- Prefill throughput, prompt tokens/s.
- Peak GPU memory during prompt load, GB.

Decoding (memory-bandwidth-bound, batch=1):
- Time-per-output-token (TPOT / inter-token latency), ms.
- Decode throughput, generated tokens/s.

Shared across conditions:
- Peak GPU memory, GB: model weights + KV-cache footprint.
- Quality block (A6): (i) WikiText-2 perplexity; (ii) one or two zero-shot probes (ARC-e and HellaSwag as the default pair, PIQA optional). Quality is reported per quantization condition, not per prompt length.

Rationale for the split: prefill is FLOP-bound and benefits little from weight compression; decoding is bandwidth-bound and benefits most. Reporting them separately is the core of the question.

--- 5. CONTROLS AND EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN ---
- Same hardware (A100-80GB), same prompt corpus, same prompt-length sweep, and same decode length across C0/C1/C2 within each model size, so differences are attributable to quantization, not data or config.
- Fixed prompt set (deterministic, versioned) so prefill/decode are paired across conditions on identical inputs.

- Paired comparisons across conditions on the same prompt corpus (not independent samples).
